summary: The exact B200 TP2 DeepSeek-V4-Flash FP4-indexer/DSpark HiCache failure could not be reproduced because the model weights, NVIDIA B200 hardware, second GPU, and reporter workload are unavailable. Current source contains post-report DeepSeek-V4 HiCache fixes and regressions, and all locally applicable focused tests passed, but that evidence is insufficient to claim the original issue fixed.

tests.what_was_measured: Current-source DeepSeek-V4 HiCache strategy dispatch, request-scoped C4 state lifecycle and isolation, staged transfer dispatch/round trips, and SWA/cache sizing boundary behavior; 76 passed, 1 skipped, 7 subtests passed.

One-gfx950 execution of generic HiCache MHA/MLA transfers and staged page-first write-back against byte-exact tensor references across layout, element-width, alignment, and page-count boundaries; 59 passed. The two DSV4 paged HiSparse tests were skipped because their source marks them CUDA-only.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 / HIP 7.2.26015. The GPU suite passed 59 applicable cases; DSV4 CUDA-only cases skipped. Raw log: reports/j-92068973cdf8/raw/gfx950_hicache_kernel_tests.log.

remaining_limitations: No NVIDIA B200 was available; gfx950 cannot validate CUDA/Blackwell-specific behavior.
Only one GPU was assigned, so the reported TP2 execution was not run.
The reporter's multi-round benchmark workload was not supplied in the issue.
The reported FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE backend, FP4 indexer, DSpark path, and full serving command were therefore not executed.
Passing generic HiCache kernels and focused unit tests do not establish that the original illegal memory access is fixed.
